Automated screen reports this URL as 'value not found' -- that is a false negative: the check reads the raw HTTP body, which for a PDF is a compressed binary stream, not searchable text. Downloaded the PDF and ran pdftotext manually: it IS live (HTTP 200, 6-page PDF) and is Mellitah Oil & Gas B.V.'s own Feb-2021 EPCIC prequalification tender ('A&E STRUCTURES, MELLITAH COMPLEX EXPANSION & CO2 MANAGEMENT INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT PROJECT'). It explicitly and separately describes the Structure A route (18in/43km to Sabratha Platform -- a different segment, not this one) and the Structure E route: 'A new gas sealine (32" to be verified during FEED) 130 km long [deliver] E Structure production to Mellitah' -- 130 km matches the sheet's recorded LengthKnown exactly. IMPORTANT CAVEAT (per brief): this is the pre-FEED design estimate. The project's later, post-FID (2023) public description at offshore-technology.com instead states a shorter, revised design -- 'A 30km-long and 36in-diameter gas pipeline will deliver production from Structure E to an existing 36in gas export pipeline from the Sabratha Platform to the Mellitah Complex' -- i.e., after FEED, Structure E ties into the EXISTING Sabratha-Mellitah trunk rather than running a new 130km line all the way to Mellitah as originally scoped. So the sheet's 130km value is real and sourced (matches this primary document exactly) but reflects an earlier design phase; the apparently 'final'/most-recent figure per offshore-technology.com is 30km. Only ONE source gives 130km specifically for the Structure E sealine (a similar, earlier 2018 mellitahog.ly scope-of-work doc gives the same ~130km distance but a 30in diameter -- same operator, not independent, so not counted as a second source). Flagging this design-stage discrepancy for the data team; staged as medium/single-source rather than fabricating a second independent confirmation of 130km specifically.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solidly confirmed — independent of GEM entirely. The wiki's own cited leads check out: jpt.spe.org (verified) and lywitness.com (Arabic, read) both describe Saipem's Aug-2023 ~$1bn EPC award covering 'laying 28km of pipelines to connect the DP3, DP4 and Sabratha platforms' plus a 5,000-t gas recovery module on DP4; mellitahog.ly is the operator's own site (context only, not cited). Independently, nsenergybusiness.com's project profile (verified, read in full) gives the precise two-segment breakdown that matches GEM's row split exactly: 'DP3 to DP4: a 14-inch cladded pipeline of 8.5km' (= sibling P6716) and 'DP4 to Sabratah to Onshore: Around 20km long 10-inch CS and a 4-inch CS pipelines... connect DP4 Platform to Sabratah Platform, then to Mellitah Onshore Plant' (= this row, P7617). That is a direct, specific match for Length=20km and Diameter='10,4in' (two parallel lines, 10in + 4in) — the automated screen flagged 'value not found' only because the source spells it as prose ('10-inch...and a 4-inch') rather than the compact GEM notation; on manual read it fully supports the recorded value. Fresh 2026 reporting (oilprice.com, libyaherald.com, both verified) independently re-confirms the '10-inch, 20km' line from Bouri/DP4 to Sabratha to Mellitah, so this is not just a 2023-era claim. Fuel=Gas and FuelSource='Bouri Field' are confirmed (attaqa.net, verified, read; matches all English coverage — associated/raw gas from the offshore Bouri field). CLASSIFICATION caveat: PipelineType='transmission' is defensible but debatable — this line carries raw/associated gas from offshore wellhead platforms (DP4) to an onshore processing complex (Mellitah) rather than finished gas between transmission hubs, which by strict convention reads more like a gathering/feeder trunk; flagging as a soft note rather than a hard concern since GEM classifies comparable large-bore field-to-plant subsea trunks as transmission elsewhere in this batch (e.g. sibling P6716) for consistency, and I don't have a clean basis to call it definitively wrong. ATTRIBUTION caveat: StartLocation is recorded as generic 'Bouri Platform' rather than the more precise 'DP4 Platform' that every source actually names as this segment's origin — not wrong (DP4 is part of the Bouri field), just looser than it could be. SPEC caveat: one secondary Arabic source, attaqa.net (verified, read closely with verbatim quotes), attributes the 8.5km/20km split differently — it says the 8.5km line runs to Sabratha and the 20km line runs on from Sabratha to the onshore station, the reverse of nsenergybusiness's DP3→DP4 (8.5km) / DP4→Sabratha→onshore (20km) mapping that GEM's row split matches. I weight nsenergybusiness (a dedicated projects-tracking profile with granular platform-to-platform detail) over attaqa's looser business-press paraphrase, and 2026 reporting's language ('Bouri field to Sabratha platform... 10-inch, 20km') sides with nsenergybusiness/GEM's mapping, so I'm not escalating this to a hard concern, but flagging the conflict for the record.
